opportunities.title: Historic buildings and structures (Preservation and Conservation)

amount.raw: Generally, £1,000 to £30,000 (average approx. £15,000). Sometimes larger sums are considered.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charity, organisation with exempt charitable status, recognised public body, Community Benefit Society, or Community Interest Company (CIC) limited by guarantee. Project must be UK based, not complete, and focus on a listed building or structure.
opportunities.summary: Grants to fund the preservation and repair of listed historic buildings, structures and architectural features, with special consideration for projects conserving and re-using buildings of outstanding importance that are at risk. Funds project costs, staff costs, fees, internships, initial exploratory work and capital costs.

opportunities.title: Places of worship (Preservation and Conservation)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Anglican churches must apply via the ChurchCare conservation grants scheme (part-funded by the Trust); all other denominations, faiths and cathedrals may apply directly to the Trust.
opportunities.summary: Grants for the conservation of historic interiors and historic objects in places of worship open for regular worship (bells, books and manuscripts, clocks, decorative plasterwork, metalwork and church plate, monuments, organs, paintings, stained glass, textiles, timberwork, wall paintings and churchyard structures), including conservation reports and environmental/technical investigations. The Trust no longer provides repair grants to places of worship open for active worship.

opportunities.title: Conservation of cultural heritage (Preservation and Conservation)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charity, organisation with exempt charitable status, recognised public body, Community Benefit Society, or Community Interest Company (CIC) limited by guarantee. Applicants must not be eligible for the grant programmes run by AIM and NMCT.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting the preservation and conservation of culturally and historically significant collections and objects including works of art, books, significant ephemera, artefacts and archives. Conservation work should be carried out by an accredited conservator, enable greater public access, and encourage paid internships and knowledge sharing.

opportunities.title: Archives Revealed
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charity, organisation with exempt charitable status, or recognised public body. Project must be UK based and not complete.
opportunities.summary: A partnership funding programme between The National Archives, The National Lottery Heritage Fund, the Pilgrim Trust and the Wolfson Foundation - the only UK grant programme dedicated to cataloguing and unlocking archival collections to ensure significant archive collections are made accessible to the public for research and enjoyment. Applications are made via the National Archives website.

opportunities.title: Research, advocacy and development fund

amount.raw: A small pot of funding is set aside for this work.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Organisations doing research, advocacy and sector development work in young women's mental health and preservation and conservation of historic buildings and collections. The Trust is currently unlikely to support further research/advocacy work in the young women's mental health field as proposals are already under development.
opportunities.summary: A fund allowing the Trust to make strategic interventions in its areas of interest (young women's mental health and preservation/conservation) where they may bring about systemic change, drive forward policy and practice, or strengthen the sector. The Trust normally builds partnerships and invites applications for initiatives it is interested in supporting.
